title: Short Stuff: Shar Pei
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Shar Pei dog breed. The hosts cover the breed's origin in China (name translating roughly to "sand skin"), its size and appearance (skin folds, muzzle, eye shape, coat colors), and the cause of the folds: excess hyaluronic acid, linked to the hyaluronic acid synthesis 2 gene, with Dr. Kirsten Lynn bladtoe of Uppsala University cited. They discuss health problems tied to the skin folds, including eye damage from skin pressing on the eyes and cornea, periodic fever syndrome (familial Shar Pei fever), and Shar Pei autoinflammatory disease (SPAID). They compare the breed's inbred problems to bulldogs, describe temperament (loyal, independent, wary of strangers and other dogs), and mention AKC guidance on training and older children. The episode ends with a call for Shar Pei owners to share their experiences.

segments.title: Opening banter and naming the breed
segments.summary: Hosts banter and settle on the topic of the Shar Pei, noting the plural spelling and that it is a dog breed that originated in China.

segments.title: Shar Pei appearance and size
segments.summary: The breed is described as a dog with huge folds of loose skin on the head, neck and shoulders, a name meaning roughly sand skin, weight of 45 to 60 pounds, a height of a couple of feet, and coat colors that vary in shades, with a prominent muzzle and small soft eyes.

segments.title: Hyaluronic acid and the cause of the wrinkles
segments.summary: The folds are explained by excess hyaluronic acid accumulating in the skin, controlled by the hyaluronic acid synthesis 2 gene. Dr. Kirsten Lynn bladtoe of Uppsala University in Sweden is cited as the source of the information.

segments.title: Temperament and care needs
segments.summary: The breed is described as loyal but independent, not very friendly with other dogs or strangers, and needing more veterinary care than an average mutt. The hosts note the health care needs tie back to the skin folds.

segments.title: Eye problems from skin folds
segments.summary: Skin folds pressing on the eyes can cause problems including blindness from pressure on the retina and damage to the cornea when a fold turns inward. The eyes can also be weaker in general.

segments.title: Periodic fever and SPAID genetic disorders
segments.summary: The hosts discuss periodic fever disease, also called familial Shar Pei fever, which causes sudden fever and listlessness and is linked to the same gene, plus Shar Pei autoinflammatory disease (SPAID), with fever, arthritis, dermatitis, ear and organ infections.

segments.title: Comparison to bulldog breeding
segments.summary: The hosts compare the Shar Pei's inherited problems to bulldogs, whose noses were bred shorter. They also recall that 19th-century bulldogs were bred to be calmer after a public outcry over their reputation for violence.

segments.title: AKC guidance and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts note American Kennel Club guidance that obedience training is recommended and that the breed may not suit young children, then invite Shar Pei owners to share their stories and close the episode.
